messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (gateway errors + timeouts). Error rate jumped to ~18% at 12:02 UTC. Paging sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: Ack — I'm on it. Can someone grab recent deploys? Any config changes in the last hour?

runtime-amy: Not that I'm aware of. No deploys in the last 2h to inference runtime. I'll start tailing the model-runner logs and the gateway.

platform-jamal: I'm seeing increased 5xx from gateway logs too. Routing layer reports HTTP 502/504 and some 500s with "upstream reset".

prod-support-leo: CS is seeing multiple customer-reported failures, some timeouts on long prompts. Ticket count climbing.

runtime-amy: Pasting the tail of model-runner stderr (stripped):
```
2026-03-14T12:03:05Z [runner] EVT memory spike pid=2345 rss=13.2G
2026-03-14T12:03:05Z [runner] ERROR segfault at 0x7f34abff, signal 11
2026-03-14T12:03:06Z [uncaught] core dumped: /opt/redwood/bin/model-runner
```

platform-jamal: nvm, I can also see OOM events on a few nodes in the cluster. nvidia-smi shows repeated GPU memory allocation failures around same timestamps.

sre-oncall: Okay this smells like the model runner process is crashing on specific requests causing gateway 5xx. Can we identify request pattern? Any correlated client IDs or prompt sizes?

runtime-amy: Correlating logs now. Early look: spikes line up with requests where prompt token counts > 12k. We don't gracefully handle very long prefix; kernel tries to allocate big KV cache and then crashes.

prod-support-leo: Customer-impact summary for triage call: ~5% of active sessions from three mid-market customers got 5xx between 12:02–12:10 UTC. No lasting data loss; retries succeed for smaller prompts.

cs-jess: I'm messaging the affected accounts with a brief note: "We’re investigating increased 5xx for long prompts in us-west-2. Temporary mitigation available."

sre-oncall: Immediate mitigations: 1) Add a routing rule to reject or truncate requests > 8k tokens with friendly 400/429. 2) Route heavy requests to a safe fallback pool (smaller model or CPU pool) until we fix. Jamal — can you push a quick traffic policy?

platform-jamal: On it. Pushing a routing-rule: `if request.tokens > 8000 then route: fallback-lowmem`. Deploying now (rolling config).

incident-bot: Config-change detected by deploy-bot: routing policy updated by platform-jamal at 12:09:32 UTC.

runtime-amy: I'm going to restart the affected model-runner pods one-at-a-time to clear coroutines and release leaked memory. I'll annotate with `hotfix/long-prompt-guard`.

prod-support-leo: Noted. Restarting pods may cause short 503 blips; I'll warn CS to expect small retries.

runtime-amy: Restart loop started. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runner -n prod --selector=pool=us-west-2-hot`

platform-jamal: Routing rule is live. Telemetry shows a drop in 5xx to ~6% within 90s after rule application.

runtime-amy: After restarting the three affected pods, I pulled core from one and ran `gdb` backtrace. Top frames: `kv_cache_alloc +0x...`, `forward_attention +0x...`, then SIGSEGV. Looks like a bounds-check regression when sequence length hits >12k.

sre-oncall: Can you share the backtrace snippet?

runtime-amy: Backtrace (sanitized):
```
#0  0x7f34aaff in kv_cache_alloc (size=...) at kv_cache.c:213
#1  0x7f34bbcc in forward_attention (ctx=...) at attention.c:987
#2  0x7f34ccdd in model_step (ctx=...) at model.c:456
#3  0x400abc in runner_handle_request (req=...) at runner.c:1208
```

prod-support-leo: Any indication this is a bad build or regression?

runtime-amy: Not a deploy; same binary has been running for days. Looks like a latent bug triggered by unusually long prefixes — maybe we never tested >10k token sequences in prod.

cs-jess: I've told customers we have a mitigation and asked them to avoid extremely long prompts for now. They asked for ETA — can we provide one?

sre-oncall: Short ETA for mitigation: immediate routing/truncate live. For full fix: need code patch + QA — estimate 48–72 hours. We'll prioritize a hotfix for sequence-length guard.

platform-jamal: Also enabling a temporary autoscaling cap so fallback pool can take load. `kubectl scale --replicas=8 deployment/model-runner-fallback -n prod` in progress.

incident-bot: Autoscaling change logged by deploy-bot at 12:12:01 UTC.

runtime-amy: Creating a small hotfix branch with an input-length guard and early 400 if > 12k tokens, plus safer kv alloc clamp. Pushing PR now: `hotfix/guard-long-prefix`

sre-oncall: Good. While we wait on PR, keep monitoring errors and customer impact. Leo — please update CS & affected customers with the short-term mitigation and ETA.

prod-support-leo: Will do. Sending updated note: "We have applied routing rules to divert very long prompts and restarted impacted services. Expect significantly reduced errors. Root cause under investigation; hotfix ETA ~48h."

runtime-amy: PR opened and CI started. Running limited regression tests against long-sequence harness.

platform-jamal: Telemetry now shows 5xx back to baseline (~0.8%) after routing and restarts. Nice work.

cs-jess: Customers acknowledged the update and appreciate the quick mitigation. One asked for an SLA credit inquiry; passing to billing.

sre-oncall: I'll keep the thread open for handoff to oncall-night. Current status: mitigation in place, traffic guarded, restarts done, fallback pool scaled. Continue monitoring; if errors spike again at >2% we wake the team.

runtime-amy: Follow-ups: instrument sequence length histogram, add unit test for >12k, and schedule native memory sanitizer run. I'll file follow-up tasks in the runbook.

incident-bot: Incident note created: `INC-20260314-1` severity: high.

sre-oncall: Thanks all. Handoff to night oncall in 1h with link to this thread and logs. I'll draft short postmortem skeleton once root cause confirmed.

prod-support-leo: Closing loop with CS — they'll reopen if customers still see issues.

cs-jess: Thanks team.

sre-oncall: Thread pinned for follow-up. Ending live mitigation phase at 12:18 UTC.

incident-bot: Thread archived to incidents channel log at 12:19:20 UTC.
